posts.text:
Despite Trump’s promises to bring down prices “on Day One,” Americans paid an average of $310 more for groceries in 2025 compared to 2024.

American families are footing the bill for Trump’s reckless policies.

Corruption is the thing that’s keeping us from passing policies that most Americans agree on. @ZachWahls knows this, and he just released a ten-point anti-corruption plan to end this rigged system.

Let’s get Zach to the Senate. We need more of this from Democrats.

Video

61% of Americans worry a great deal about health care access and affordability.

But thanks to Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill, health care costs have skyrocketed across the country, and access has been rolled back. He is making our health care system worse.

news.gallup.com/poll/707732/…

Trump's recent priorities?

Asking Congress for $200 billion to pay for his illegal war in Iran.

Adding his signature to paper currencies while families struggle every day to afford groceries and gas.

Building a $400 million, gold-encrusted White House ballroom.

Congratulations to @AnaliliaForNJ on her big win in NJ-11!

Analilia has been fighting for working people her whole career—and she stood up to dark money interests to bring this fight to Congress. I'm thrilled to fight side-by-side together.


Analilia Mejia for NJ (@AnaliliaForNJ)

To NJ-11: THANK YOU!

I’m honored to be elected your next Congresswoman.

This victory belongs to all of us! We won by organizing our communities, and that work doesn’t stop now. 

As your Congresswoman, I’ll fight f

Sports streaming consolidation—like recent deals between Disney, Fubo, ESPN, NFL Network, & MLB TV—increases costs for fans while affecting their ability to watch their local teams.

I’m pushing to protect consumers against corporate consolidation and streamflation.

Companies that have paid settlements to the Trump Library Fund:

ABC: $15 million
Meta: $22 million
X: $10 million
Paramount: $16 million

That original Library Fund has now been dissolved. So where has all that money gone?

Trump is costing Americans more than $86 BILLION each year by dismantling the programs, rules, and tax credits that used to put money back in the pockets of working families.

Trump has broken his promise to lower costs, all while enriching billionaires and the wealthy.

Tesla paid $0 in federal income taxes in 2025, despite making $5.7 billion.

This Tax Day, remember that you have paid more in taxes than a multi-billion dollar company—all thanks to corporate tax breaks from Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill.
Community note: Tesla reported $0 in current federal income tax for 2025 due to net operating loss carryforwards from prior years and longstanding tax credits like R&D, not specific corporate tax breaks from Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill. sec.gov/Archives/ed

Self-interested billionaires helped send Donald Trump to the White House, and on Tax Day they're enjoying a return on their investment.

His Big Beautiful Bill delivered $1 trillion in tax cuts to the top 1 percent.

For years, Live Nation and Ticketmaster: 

- Overcharged fans 
- Piled on junk fees
- Provided horrible service
- Monopolized the live event industry 

Today, a jury called it what it is: ILLEGAL.

Ending Direct File will cost taxpayers billions of dollars—money that will flow into tax prep companies. It's time to stop giant companies from profiting off a process the government once made free. I have a bill to get Congress to reverse Trump’s decision to cancel Direct File.

A Boston public school teacher is paying a higher tax rate than Jeff Bezos is today.

That's flat-out wrong.

My Wealth Tax for ultra-millionaires and billionaires will finally right the wrongs of our tax code so that the rich pay their fair share.

Everyone in America supports filing their taxes directly with the IRS for free—everyone but Trump & executives at giant tax prep companies like Intuit-TurboTax, who teamed up to cancel Direct File. 

(What a coincidence: Intuit donated $1 million to Trump’s inauguration.)

It's Tax Day in America.

Reminder: The average taxpayer pays 13% of their income in taxes. The wealthiest 400 families in the U.S. pay just 8% of their income in taxes.

It’s time to make the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share.

It’s time to pass a wealth tax.
